:JUDGMENT:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioners against Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.60,00,000/- for the death of Sri. Manoj Kumar Ram S/o Late Kishnath Ram in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 05.12.2023 at about 9.15 p.m., when the husband of the Petitioner No.1 by name Manoj Kumar Ram was standing in front of Karnataka bank, Kaggalipura village, Kanakapura - Bengaluru main road, Uttrahalli Hobli, Bengaluru, at that time, one KTM Duke motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-KA-0625 SCCH 15 4 MVC No.149/2024 ridden by Gita Devi vs Sunil Kumar H S on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188947831/
2 its rider came in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed to the Manoj Kumar Ram.

sentences.text: Due to the impact, Manoj Kumar Ram had sustained grievous injuries to all over the body.

3. Immediately after the accident, the Manoj Kumar Ram was taken to Government Hospital,
Kaggalipura and after first aid treatment he was shifted to Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru.
But, during the course of treatment, he was succumbed to the injuries on 06.12.2023.
The Petitioners had spent about Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, nourishment, transportation of dead body and funeral obsequies.
Prior to the date of the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and he was working as a Mason and was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
The Petitioners were entirely depending upon the income of the deceased.
Due to the death of Manoj Kumar Ram, the Petitioners have lost their bread earner.
The Respondent No.1 is the owner and the Respondent SCCH 15 5 MVC No.149/2024 No.2 is the insurer of the offending KTM Duke motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-KA-0625.

Therefore,
the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.

4. In pursuance of service of Notice to the Respondents, both Respondent No.1 and 2 had appeared before the Court through their respective Counsels and filed their Objection statements to the main Petition.

The Respondent No.1 in his Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and also the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle and also the death of the deceased Manoj Kumar Ram in the said accident.

Further he contended that the rider of the motorcycle was proceeding slowly and cautiously on the extreme left side of the road by following all the traffic rules, at that time, all of a sudden the deceased was suddenly crossing the road without observing any traffic rules and regulations.
The alleged accident occurred solely due to the SCCH 15 6 MVC No.149/2024 carelessness of the deceased and not due to the rashness and negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle.
Further he contended that offending vehicle was insured with the Respondent No.2 and the policy was valid at the time of the accident.
Hence, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
On these grounds, the Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the Petition against him.

The Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle and also the death of the deceased Manoj Kumar Ram in the said accident.
Further it admitted the issuance of policy in respect of offending vehicle and its validity at the time of accident.
Further it contended that the rider of the offending motorcycle does not hold valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
Hence, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
On these grounds, the Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the Petition against it.

On the basis of the rival pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following Issues:

opposite to Karnataka Bank, Kaggalipura village, Kanakapur - Bengaluru road,
Uttarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru South, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the KTM Duke motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-KA-0625?
2) Whether the Petitioners further prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Manoj Kumar Ram?
3) Whether the Petitioners are entitled for the compensation as prayed for?

sentences.text: In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, PW1 has relied on Ex.P-1 to Ex.P15.

Ex.P-1 & 2 are the True copies of FIR and Complaint which was lodged by the son of the deceased, the Kaggalipura Police have registered the case against the rider of KTM Duke motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 01-KA-0625 for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC.
Ex.P3 is the Spot mahazar and Spot Sketch which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar and sketch at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P4 is the IMV SCCH 15 10 MVC No.149/2024 report which shows that the accident does not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle.
Ex.P5 is the Inquest Mahazar.
Ex.P6 is the PM report which shows the cause of death is due to Spinal Cord injury sustained.

Ex.P-7 is the true copy of the Charge-Sheet which shows that the Kaggalipura Police have submitted Charge-sheet against the rider of the offending motorcycle for the offences punishable under Sec. 279, 338 and 304(A) of IPC.
Ex.P8 to 15 are the Police Notice, Reply and Aadhaar cards.
12. PW.1 is subjected for cross examination by the learned counsel for Respondent No.2.

But,
nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of PW.1.
To rebut the evidence of PW.1, The Respondent No.1 got examined himself as RW.1 and got marked 4 documents at Ex.R1 to 4.
In the cross- examination by the Learned Counsel for the Petitioner, he admitted that neither he nor Santhosh Kumar had challenged the Charge-sheet.
It is pertinent to note here that the Spot mahazar clearly shows that the accident has occurred on the SCCH 15 11 MVC No.149/2024 Western side footpath.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioners have proved the rash and negligent riding of the offending motorcycle and in the said accident, the husband of PW.1 was succumbed to the injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 is "in the Affirmative."

13. Issue No.2 and 3: Both these Issues are taken together for common discussion as they are interlinked with each other and to avoid repetition of facts.
14.
The Petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased, Petitioner No.2 to 4 are the children and Petitioner No.5 is the mother of the deceased Manoj Kumar Ram.
To prove their relationship with the deceased, PW.1 has produced her Aadhaar card and Aadhaar cards of deceased and other Petitioners at Ex.P.10 to 15.
The said documents shows the relationship between the Petitioners and the deceased.

As the Petitioners are the LRs of deceased Manoj Kumar Ram, they entitled for the SCCH 15 12 MVC No.149/2024 compensation.
15.
In the petition, the age of the deceased was shown as 47 years and deceased was working as a Mason and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
But, PW.1 has not produced any document in this regard.

Therefore, in the absence of income proof, the notional income to be taken at Rs.16,000/-
per month for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
16. Further, the Petitioners stated the age of the deceased Manoj Kumar Ram as 47 years at the time of the accident.
PW.1 has produced Ex.P.10 i.e., the Aadhaar Card of the deceased Manoj Kumar Ram which shows his date of birth as 01.01.1976.
The alleged accident was occurred on 05.12.2023.
That means, as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased Manoj Kumar Ram was 47 years, 11 months and 04 days.

Hence, the age of the deceased Manoj Kumar Ram to be taken at 48 years for Gita Devi vs Sunil Kumar H S on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188947831/

sentences.text: With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioners are entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF CONSORTIUM, COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF ESTATE, COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUNERAL EXPENSES:
18.
The deceased has left behind him his wife, children and mother.

The Petitioner No.1 is the wife,
Petitioner No.2 to 4 are the children and the Petitioner No.5 is the mother and they are considered as dependents on the deceased.

At this juncture, I would like to go through principles laid down in the decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others) wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has pleased to observed that:
"Loss of estate has to be compensated by awarding Rupees 15,000/-, loss of consortium should be Rupees 40,000/- and funeral expenses should be Rupees 15,000/-".

sentences.text: SCCH 15 14 MVC No.149/2024 It is further observed that the aforesaid Judgment amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
The said Judgment was rendered on 30.10.2017.

By applying the said observation made in the aforesaid case, since, more than 6 years lapsed from the date of Order, the consortium fixed in the said case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Further, the loss of estate and funeral expenses also extended to Rs.18,150/- each.

19. As this Court has already observed that the Petitioner No.1 to 5 are the wife, children and mother of the deceased Manoj Kumar Ram, they are entitled for a sum of Rupees 48,400/- each towards loss of consortium and Rupees 18,150/- towards loss of estate and Rupees 18,150/- towards funeral expenses.
IV. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF LOVE AND AFFECTION,
20.
Petitioner No.1 is the wife and she lost her husband's SCCH 15 15 MVC No.149/2024 love and care and support.
Petitioner No.2 to 4 are the children and they lost their father's love and care and the Petitioner No.5 is the mother and she lost her son's love and care.
Bearing in mind the relationship of the Petitioners with the deceased, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS TRANSPORTATION OF DEAD BODY:
21. The Petitioners might have spent some amount towards transportation of body of the deceased.
Hence, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.5,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

Yes: there cannot be distinction where there is evidence of income and where minimum income is determined on guesswork: executing Court directed to respondent compute entitlement of claimants by adding 40 per cent of income for future prospect and make corresponding deduction towards personal expenses".

The decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others) wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has pleased to observed that: In case self employed or person on fixed salary the addition should be 25% when the age is between 40 to 50 years".

26. Regarding Liability : This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent riding on the part of the rider of the offending KTM Duke motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-KA-0625.
In this case, SCCH 15 20 MVC No.149/2024 the Respondent No.1 is the owner and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award amount.
The Respondent No.2, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1, has to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
